description: A theme swaps three variables only: canvas, ink, accent. The grammar (2px borders, zero-blur shadows, sharp corners, type pairing, spacing) never changes. This is what makes one design language produce many products.

themes.name: Paper Yellow
themes.fits: Agent workspaces, developer tools, the house default

themes.name: Night Yellow
themes.fits: Dashboards, monitoring, anything that lives on a second monitor at night
themes.note: Warm black and warm white. Never #000, never cool grey. Text on the accent stays ink-dark (#1c1915).

themes.name: Paper Pink
themes.fits: Creative tools, community products, anything that wants warmth without going soft
themes.note: The canvas carries a blush cast and surface.raised is pulled further toward the accent, so the theme reads pink at a glance rather than only at the buttons. Hard borders keep it from turning sweet.

themes.name: Paper Orange
themes.fits: Food, community, lifestyle, anything that wants more warmth than the default

themes.name: Paper Cyan
themes.fits: Technical tools and infrastructure. Cool accent against warm paper reads as precise.

themes.name: Paper Lime
themes.fits: Health, sustainability, finance with a positive frame

themes.name: Cool Lavender
themes.fits: B2B and professional products. The only cool-canvas theme; use it when warm cream reads as too playful.

steps: Pick an accent with a luminance high enough that ink text on it clears 4.5:1. Test before committing.
Keep canvas near-white with a hue cast (warm cream by default). Fully saturated canvases collapse the block structure.
Derive surface.raised as canvas nudged toward the accent hue by a few percent, surface.high as canvas nudged toward white.

Set surface.plain, the fill for inputs, secondary buttons and table bodies. On a light canvas it is white; on a dark canvas it must be a raised dark, never white, or every input turns into a glare panel.
Set muted, the secondary text color, and check it against the canvas. The default cool slate only works on a light canvas.
Keep ink a near-black that shares the canvas hue family. Warm canvas gets warm ink, cool canvas gets cool ink.
For a dark theme, invert canvas and ink but keep both warm or both cool. Never invert the accent, and never invert onFill: text on colored blocks stays dark.
Leave the categorical palette alone. It carries status and identity, not brand.
deriveNewTheme.verify: node tools/contrast.mjs [--dark] <canvas> <ink> <accent> [surface] to check a candidate, or node tools/contrast.mjs with no arguments to re-check every shipped theme. Pass --dark for a dark candidate, or the accent will be measured against the wrong ink.

print.note: A theme in print is a paper stock plus one spot ink. See references/print.md section 3.

paperStock.paper-yellow: Warm uncoated cream, oatmeal or natural. Let the sheet carry the canvas color rather than flooding a tint.
paperStock.night-yellow: Does not translate cheaply. Flooding a dark sheet is expensive and dries badly. Prefer a dark uncoated stock with an opaque white or metallic ink, and treat it as a different job.
paperStock.paper-pink: Warm uncoated in blush or a natural cream. Do not chase the canvas with a flood tint; a lightly toned stock plus the spot does the work.
paperStock.paper-orange: Warm uncoated, same family as paper-yellow.
paperStock.paper-cyan: Warm uncoated. The cool accent against warm paper is the whole point.
paperStock.paper-lime: Warm uncoated or a natural recycled sheet.
paperStock.cool-lavender: The one theme that wants a cool or bright white sheet.

spotStartingPoints.note: Starting points for a conversation with your printer. Confirm against a physical swatch book, never against a screen.

print.proof: Anything with a saturated accent needs a physical proof on the actual stock before the run. Screens lie about exactly the colors this palette leans on.
